ui_bugs.issue: CRITICAL Rules-of-Hooks violation — the previous iteration's suggestion to hide the orb on /sign-in was implemented by adding `if (hidden) return null;` at line 35, BEFORE `useRef(new Animated.Value(...))` at lines 38-39 and two `useEffect` hooks. The moment the user logs in (hidden flips true→false), React throws 'Rendered more hooks than during the previous render' and shows a full red screen for EVERY authenticated user (Papa AND Admin). Reproduced 100% before the fix. Fixed by moving all hooks above the `if (hidden) return null;` guard.

integration_issues.issue: On react-native-web, Alert.alert with multiple buttons falls back to window.confirm and with one button falls back to window.alert — in headless Playwright the dialog fires but our page.on('dialog') listener does not observe every case reliably. The important guard (openModify() short-circuits BEFORE navigation) IS correctly wired: URL stays on /shipment/<id> after Modify tap, no navigation to /shipment/new occurs. Functionally correct; only the user-facing Alert visibility on web is a react-native-web quirk (native mobile Alerts work fine).

rca_of_issue: Root cause of the red-screen crash: In iteration 58 (Phase 1), the testing agent suggested hiding the voice orb on unauthenticated routes. The main agent added `const hidden = !auth.user || (pathname||'').includes('sign-in'); if (hidden) return null;` — but placed it at line 34-35, BEFORE the `useRef(new Animated.Value(0.6))` on line 38 and two useEffect hooks. On /sign-in the component returned early → 0 hooks called. Immediately after login, the same component instance re-renders with `hidden=false` and calls 2 useRefs + 2 useEffects → React detects the hook-count change and throws 'Rendered more hooks than during the previous render'. Fix: moved the `if (hidden) return null;` block AFTER all four hooks so React sees a stable hook count on every render. Verified by logging in as both Papa (bsingh) and Admin (kishan) — no more Rules-of-Hooks errors in console, no red screen, all downstream Phase-2 flows now testable.
